results.title: Finite-index normal subgroups are closed when the completion map is onto

If the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is surjective, then every normal subgroup of finite index in $P$ is closed in $P$.

results.title: Strongly complete profinite groups via the profinite completion

results.title: Character values at inverses are complex conjugates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi_\rho$. For every $g \in G$, $\chi_\rho(g^{-1}) = \overline{\chi_\rho(g)}$.

results.title: Character of the dual representation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $\rho^*$ be its dual representation. For every $g \in G$, the character of $\rho^*$ at $g$ is the complex conjugate of the character of $\rho$ at $g$: $\chi_{\rho^*}(g) = \overline{\chi_\rho(g)}$.

results.title: Class inner product

results.title: Character criterion for irreducibility

results.title: Consecutive primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Natural numbers $p$ and $q$ are consecutive primes when $p$ and $q$ are prime, $p < q$, and every prime $r$ satisfies $r \le p$ or $q \le r$; that is, no prime lies strictly between $p$ and $q$.

results.title: Block of consecutive primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $l$ of natural numbers is a block of consecutive primes when $l$ is nonempty, every entry of $l$ is prime, $l$ is strictly increasing, and every two adjacent entries of $l$ are consecutive primes.

results.title: Restricted block of consecutive primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a predicate on natural numbers. A list $l$ of natural numbers is a block of consecutive primes restricted by $P$ when $l$ is a block of consecutive primes and every entry of $l$ satisfies $P$.

results.title: Prime gap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p_0 = 2$, $p_1 = 3$, $p_2 = 5, \dots$ be the primes in increasing order, indexed from $0$. For a natural number $n$, the prime gap at $n$ is $p_{n+1} - p_n$.

results.title: Liminf of prime gaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. The liminf of prime gaps is $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; the value $\infty$ is allowed.

results.title: Successive primes in the enumeration are consecutive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $p_n$ and $p_{n+1}$ are consecutive primes: both are prime, $p_n < p_{n+1}$, and no prime lies strictly between them.

results.title: Prime gaps are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $g_n > 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, including $n = 0$.

results.title: Prime gaps after the first are at least two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. For every $n \ge 1$, $g_n \ge 2$.

results.title: The liminf of prime gaps is at least two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n \ge 2$, where the liminf is taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.

results.title: When the liminf of prime gaps is at most a given bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order, let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap, and let $L = \liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every natural number $B$, $L \le B$ if and only if $g_n \le B$ for infinitely many $n$.

results.title: Finite liminf of prime gaps and bounded gaps between primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order, let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap, and let $L = \liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. Then $L \ne \infty$ if and only if there is a natural number $B > 0$ such that infinitely many primes $p$ admit a prime $q$ with $p < q$ and $q - p \le B$.

results.title: A prime gap equals two exactly at a twin prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $g_n = 2$ if and only if $p_n + 2$ is prime.

results.title: The liminf of prime gaps is two exactly when there are infinitely many twin primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n = 2$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, if and only if there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2$ is also prime.

results.title: Lowering the smoothness keeps the inner product
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Conformal scaling of a Riemannian metric
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a manifold $B$, let $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian metric on $E$, and let $u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a $C^n$ function with $u(b) > 0$ for every $b \in B$. The conformal scaling of $g$ by $u$ is the $C^n$ Riemannian metric $u g$ on $E$ whose inner product on each fiber $E_b$ is $u(b)$ times the inner product of $g$ on $E_b$.

results.title: Inner product of a conformally scaled metric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a manifold $B$, let $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian metric on $E$, with inner product $g_b$ on the fiber $E_b$, and let $u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a $C^n$ function with $u(b) > 0$ for every $b \in B$. Then the conformal scaling $u g$ of $g$ by $u$ satisfies $(u g)_b(v, w) = u(b)\, g_b(v, w)$ for every $b \in B$ and all $v, w \in E_b$.

results.title: A conformal factor at a point is positive

Let $u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ and $b \in B$. If $g'_b(v, w) = u(b)\, g_b(v, w)$ for all $v, w \in E_b$ and $E_b$ contains a nonzero vector, then $u(b) > 0$.

results.title: Pole multiplicity vanishes where the function is not meromorphic

results.title: Pole multiplicity vanishes at points of nonnegative order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let the order of $f$ at $z$ be its meromorphic order, an element of $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ that is $0$ by convention when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. results.title: Pole multiplicity is nonzero exactly at negative order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let the order of $f$ at $z$ be its meromorphic order, an element of $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ that is $0$ by convention when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. The pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is nonzero if and only if this order is negative, that is, if and only if $f$ has a pole at $z$.

results.title: Pole multiplicity via the divisor
results.caption: Theorem

Let $D(z)$ be the value at $z$ of the divisor of $f$ on $U$, that is, the order of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ when that order is infinite. Then the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ equals $\max(0, -D(z))$.

results.title: Membership in the pole set of a fundamental parallelogram

Then $z$ lies in the pole set of $f$ in the fundamental parallelogram of $L$ with vertex $\alpha$ if and only if $z$ lies in that parallelogram and the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is nonzero.

results.title: Finitely many poles in a fundamental parallelogram

results.summary: Let $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$ (a colored multiset). Then $s$ is a perfect $m$-cover of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ for some $m$ if and only if for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ some $s_i$ has additive order $2^j$.

results.title: Binomial coefficient with rational upper argument
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rational number $r$ and a natural number $k$, the generalized binomial coefficient is the rational number $\binom{r}{k} = r(r-1)\cdots(r-k+1)/k!$, which is $1$ for $k = 0$.

results.title: Admissible parameters for the (p,q)-Patalan numbers
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An admissible parameter pair for the $(p,q)$-Patalan numbers is a pair of natural numbers $p$ and $q$ with $p > 1$ and $0 < q < p$.

results.title: The (p,q)-Patalan numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$ with $p > 1$ and $0 < q < p$, the $(p,q)$-Patalan number with index $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is the rational number $b(n) = -p^{2n+1} \binom{n - q/p}{n+1}$, where $\binom{r}{k} = r(r-1)\cdots(r-k+1)/k!$ is the binomial coefficient with rational upper argument $r$.

results.title: The (p,q)-super Patalan numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$ with $p > 1$ and $0 < q < p$, and natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the $(p,q)$-super Patalan number is the rational number $Q(i,j) = (-1)^j p^{2(i+j)} \binom{i - q/p}{i+j}$, where $\binom{r}{k} = r(r-1)\cdots(r-k+1)/k!$ is the binomial coefficient with rational upper argument $r$.

results.title: Super Patalan numbers of order p
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p > 1$ and natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the super Patalan number of order $p$ is the $(p,q)$-super Patalan number with $q = 1$, that is, the rational number $(-1)^j p^{2(i+j)} \binom{i - 1/p}{i+j}$, where $\binom{r}{k} = r(r-1)\cdots(r-k+1)/k!$ is the binomial coefficient with rational upper argument $r$.

results.title: Entries of the infinite Pascal matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the entry of the infinite Pascal matrix in row $i$ and column $j$ is the binomial coefficient $\binom{i}{j}$.

results.title: Column generating functions of the Pascal matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $j$ and a real number $x$, the column generating function of the infinite Pascal matrix is $\alpha_j(x) = \sum_{i \ge 0} \binom{i}{j} x^i$, where $\binom{i}{j}$ is the entry in row $i$ and column $j$; the sum is taken to be $0$ when the series is not summable.

results.title: Closed form of the Pascal column generating functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $j$ and every real number $x$ with $|x| < 1$, the column generating function $\alpha_j$ of the infinite Pascal matrix satisfies $\alpha_j(x) = x^j / (1 - x)^{j+1}$.

results.title: Summing the Pascal column generating functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$ with $|x| < 1/2$, the sum $\sum_{j \ge 0} \alpha_j(x)$ of the column generating functions of the infinite Pascal matrix equals $\sum_{j \ge 0} \sum_{i \ge 0} \binom{i}{j} x^i$, where $\binom{i}{j}$ is the entry in row $i$ and column $j$, and it also equals $\sum_{j \ge 0} x^j / (1 - x)^{j+1}$.

results.title: Reversing the order of summation in the Pascal matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$ with $|x| < 1/2$, writing $\binom{i}{j}$ for the entry of the infinite Pascal matrix in row $i$ and column $j$, we have $\sum_{j \ge 0} \sum_{i \ge 0} \binom{i}{j} x^i = \sum_{i \ge 0} \sum_{j \ge 0} \binom{i}{j} x^i$, and this sum equals $\frac{1}{1 - x} \sum_{j \ge 0} \left(\frac{x}{1 - x}\right)^j$.

results.title: Summing the Pascal matrix row by row
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$ with $|x| < 1/2$, writing $\binom{i}{j}$ for the entry of the infinite Pascal matrix in row $i$ and column $j$, we have $\sum_{i \ge 0} x^i \sum_{j=0}^{i} \binom{i}{j} = \frac{1}{1 - 2x}$.

results.title: Total generating function of the Pascal matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$ with $|x| < 1/2$, the sum $\sum_{j \ge 0} \alpha_j(x)$ of the column generating functions of the infinite Pascal matrix equals $\sum_{i \ge 0} (2x)^i$, and $\sum_{i \ge 0} (2x)^i = \frac{1}{1 - 2x}$.

results.title: Same block after merging two blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j, x, y \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $x$ and $y$ lie in the same block after merging the blocks of $i$ and $j$ if either $x$ and $y$ lie in the same block of $P$, or each of $x$ and $y$ lies in the block of $i$ or in the block of $j$. For singleton blocks $\{i\}$ and $\{j\}$ this joins them into the block $\{i, j\}$.

results.title: Crossing after merging two blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The partition obtained from $P$ by merging the blocks of $i$ and $j$ has a crossing if there are $a < b < c < d$ in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $a$ and $c$ lie in one of its blocks and $b$ and $d$ lie in a different one of its blocks.

results.title: Marriageable singles partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a marriageable singles partition if it has two distinct singleton blocks $\{i\}$ and $\{j\}$ such that the partition obtained from $P$ by joining them into the block $\{i, j\}$ has no crossing.

results.title: Number of marriageable singles partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $M_n$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that are marriageable singles partitions.

results.title: Number of lonely singles partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $L_n$ is the number of lonely singles partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, that is, of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that are not marriageable singles partitions.

results.title: Small values of the marriageable singles count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \le 1$, the number of marriageable singles partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $M_n = 0$: a marriageable singles partition needs two distinct points.

results.title: Small values of the lonely singles count

results.summary: The numbers of lonely singles partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ for $n = 0$ and $n = 1$ are $L_0 = 1$ and $L_1 = 1$.

results.title: Noncrossing partitions by number of blocks and of singleton blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $m$ and $k$, $NC_{n,m,k}$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that have exactly $m$ blocks, exactly $k$ of which are singletons.

results.title: Base value of the noncrossing block and singleton count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exactly one noncrossing partition of the empty set has $0$ blocks, $0$ of which are singletons, namely the empty partition; that is, $NC_{0,0,0} = 1$, where $NC_{n,m,k}$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $m$ blocks of which $k$ are singletons.

results.title: Unique subgraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same vertex set $V$. Then $G$ is a unique subgraph of $H$ if exactly one subgraph of $H$ is isomorphic to $G$. Here a subgraph of $H$ means a spanning subgraph: a graph on $V$ all of whose edges are edges of $H$ (not necessarily induced).

results.title: Number of unique subgraphs

results.title: Many unique subgraphs (Erdős Problem 426)

The statement is that there is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ some graph $H$ on $n$ vertices has $u(H) \ge c \cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}} / n!$.

results.title: Negation of the Erdős Problem 426 statement

results.title: Erdős Problem 426 is false (Bradač–Christoph)

results.title: Declared polynomial time for timed deciders
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to a Boolean $f(x)$ together with a declared time $t_f(x) \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ decides in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that $t_f(x) \le p(|x|)$ for every list $x$ of Booleans, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$.

results.title: Declared polynomial time for timed functions on bitstrings
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to an output list $f(x)$ of Booleans together with a declared time $t_f(x) \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ computes in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that, for every list $x$ of Booleans, both $t_f(x)$ and the length of $f(x)$ are at most $p(|x|)$, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$.

results.title: Verifiers with polynomial declared time
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A timed verifier $V$, which assigns to each pair of bit strings $(x, w)$ (an input and a witness) a timed computation returning a Boolean, runs in declared polynomial time when there is a polynomial $q$ with natural coefficients such that the declared time of $V(x, w)$ is at most $q(|x| + |w|)$ for all $x$ and $w$.

results.title: Verifying a decision problem with a witness bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A timed verifier $V$, which assigns to each pair of bit strings $(x, w)$ (an input and a witness) a timed computation returning a Boolean, verifies a decision problem $L$ with witness bound $p$, a polynomial with natural coefficients, when for every bit string $x$, $L(x)$ holds if and only if there is a witness $w$ with $|w| \le p(|x|)$ such that $V(x, w)$ returns true.

results.title: Declared-time many-one reduction by a timed function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems and let $f$ be a timed function that maps each list $x$ of Booleans to a list $f(x)$ of Booleans together with a declared time. Then $f$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$ when $f$ computes in declared polynomial time and $L_1(x) = L_2(f(x))$ for every list $x$ of Booleans.

results.title: Every decision problem has a timed decider in declared polynomial time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every decision problem $L$ there is a timed function $f$ from lists of Booleans to Booleans that decides in declared polynomial time and whose output $f(x)$ equals $L(x)$ for every list $x$ of Booleans.

results.title: A decider with polynomial declared time gives a verifier with polynomial declared time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a timed decider $f$ on bit strings has declared time bounded by a polynomial in the input length, then the verifier that sends an input $x$ and a witness $w$ to $f(x)$, ignoring $w$, has declared time bounded by a polynomial in $|x| + |w|$.

results.title: A decider is a verifier with witness bound zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem and let $f$ be a timed decider whose return value on every bit string $x$ equals $L(x)$. Then the verifier that sends an input $x$ and a witness $w$ to $f(x)$, ignoring $w$, verifies $L$ with the zero polynomial as witness bound, so only the empty witness is allowed.

results.title: Declared-time many-one reduction is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every decision problem $L$, the timed identity function, which returns its input with declared time $0$, is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L$ to $L$.

results.title: Declared-time many-one reductions compose
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$, $L_2$ and $L_3$ be decision problems. If $f_1$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$ and $f_2$ is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_2$ to $L_3$, then the timed function that on input $x$ returns $f_2(f_1(x))$, with declared time the declared time of $f_1$ on $x$ plus that of $f_2$ on $f_1(x)$, is a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_3$.

results.title: Declared polynomial time is preserved under precomposition with a reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems, let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$, and let $g$ be a timed function from lists of Booleans to Booleans that decides in declared polynomial time. Then the timed function that on input $x$ returns $g(f(x))$, with declared time the declared time of $f$ on $x$ plus that of $g$ on $f(x)$, decides in declared polynomial time.

results.title: A declared-time reduction followed by a decider for the target decides the source
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems, let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$, and let $g$ be a timed function from lists of Booleans to Booleans whose output on every list $y$ is $L_2(y)$. Then for every list $x$ of Booleans, the timed function that runs $f$ on $x$ and then $g$ on its output returns $L_1(x)$.

results.title: A timed decider with polynomial-time output function gives membership in P
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem and let $f$ assign to each bit string $x$ a timed computation, that is, a Boolean return value together with a declared time in $\mathbb{N}$, whose return value equals $L(x)$ for every $x$. If the function sending $x$ to the return value of $f(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, then $L$ belongs to the class P.

results.title: A timed verifier with polynomial-time output function puts its language in NP
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem, $p$ a polynomial with natural-number coefficients, and $V$ a timed function from pairs of lists of Booleans to Booleans that verifies $L$ with witness bound $p$. If the function sending $(x, w)$ to the output of $V$ on $(x, w)$ is polynomial-time computable by a Turing machine for the canonical bitstring encodings, then $L$ is in NP.

results.title: From declared-time to polynomial-time many-one reductions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be decision problems and let $f$ be a declared-time many-one reduction from $L_1$ to $L_2$. If the function sending $x$ to the output of $f$ on $x$ is polynomial-time computable by a Turing machine for the canonical bitstring encodings, then $L_1$ reduces to $L_2$ by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function (sojourn density), time in units of `2N` generations (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4): `G(p, x) = 2 (1 - p) / (1 - x)` for `x ≤ p` and `G(p, x) = 2 p / x` for `p < x`. In the diffusion reading, for `0 < x < 1`, `G(p, x) dx` is the expected time a neutral allele started at frequency `p` spends at frequencies in `(x, x + dx)` before loss or fixation.

results.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous `g` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the function `u(q) = ∫ x in 0..1, G(q, x) g(x)` solves the neutral backward equation `L_0 u = -g` at `p`. In the diffusion reading, `u(p)` is the expected value of `∫₀^T g(X_t) dt` up to the absorption time `T`.

results.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for an absent allele
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Boundary value at `0`: an allele that is absent spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so `∫ x in 0..1, G(0, x) g(x) = 0`.

results.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for a fixed allele
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Boundary value at `1`: a fixed allele spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so `∫ x in 0..1, G(1, x) g(x) = 0`.

results.title: Mean absorption time as a sojourn integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `p ∈ [0, 1]`, the total expected sojourn time `∫ x in 0..1, G(p, x)` is the Kimura–Ohta mean absorption time `-2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))` (units of `2N` generations).
